rewrites.comment: Build output is real files or nothing. A client still holding an old chunk name after a deploy has to get a 404 it can recover from, never the index shell answered as JavaScript — that is a module parse error and a white screen. Rewriting the path to itself leaves a real file alone and lets a missing one 404.

Screens are state, not routes, and the router is hash-based, so the server only ever sees / in normal use. This is the safety net for a stray deep link, which should land on the app rather than a dead end. Anything with a file extension is left alone so a genuinely missing asset still 404s.

headers.comment: Mirror of the /* block in public/_headers — change one, change the other. style-src-attr is the load-bearing directive: css() becomes a React style prop, so the whole app is inline style ATTRIBUTES, which CSP Level 3 governs with style-src-attr rather than style-src. style-src-elem stays locked to 'self'; the plain style-src line is the fallback for browsers too old for the granular pair, so they degrade to a weaker policy rather than to an unstyled page. No wss: — nothing calls db.channel(), so Supabase realtime never opens a socket.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src-elem 'self'; style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self' data:; manifest-src 'self'; worker-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.frankfurter.app https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org https://overpass-api.de https://prices.openfoodfacts.org https://world.openfoodfacts.org https://*.supabase.co; upgrade-insecure-requests
geolocation=(self), camera=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=(), display-capture=(), browsing-topics=()

headers.comment: The worker decides when everything else updates, so it must never be the stale thing.
A host that does not know .webmanifest guesses application/octet-stream, and a manifest served as a download is a manifest the installer ignores.
Content-hashed by the build, so they can be cached forever.
same-site, not same-origin, so apex and www both keep working. This does not stop anyone copying a photograph; it stops another site using it from your server.
